hook.line: Someone steals your wallet on the bus, or you cut your finger slicing guava. In English, everything is "my". Spanish already knows whose it is.
hook.es: Me robaron la billetera en el bus.
hook.en: They stole my wallet on the bus.

examples.en: Does your head hurt? (to a friend)

examples.es: Me robaron el celular en el bus.
examples.en: They stole my phone on the bus.

rule:
English says *my finger*, *his wallet*. Spanish uses *el*, *la*, *los* or *las*, and the small word *me*, *te*, *le*, *nos* or *les* says whose it is:

*Me corté el dedo.* (I cut my finger)
*Le robaron la billetera.* (his wallet)

You already know the idea from *se me cayó*. The person is the one things happen to.

Use it for body parts, clothes and things you carry:
*Me duele la espalda.*
*Se lavó las manos.*

Be careful: if you say *mi dedo*, it sounds like the finger belongs to you but you are not the one affected. For your own body, use the small word.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the possessive dative. The indirect object stands in for *my*, *your* and *his*.

options: Does your head hurt? (to a friend)
They stole your phone. (to a friend)
I wash your hair. (to a friend)
They took your bag. (to a friend)

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: Me corté ___ dedo. (el / mi) I cut my finger.
yourTurn.why: The small word *me* already says whose, so you use *el*.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: Le robaron ___ billetera. (la / su) They stole his wallet.
yourTurn.why: *Le* says whose it is, so you use *la*.
*Me* is whose, and *el pelo* is the thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Does your head hurt?
Make it about her: Me lavo las manos.
yourTurn.why: For her, the small word is *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about us: Me robaron el celular.
yourTurn.why: Only the small word changes, to *nos*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Me* already says whose finger it is, so you do not repeat it with *mi*.
The hair is yours and you are doing it to yourself, so Spanish uses *me* plus *el*.
*Le* says whose head it is. Use *la*, not *su*.
Better with the small word: *me* shows it happened to you, and *la* takes the place of *mi*.

personal: Tell us about something that happened to you or your things: a cut, a bump, something taken or lost. Write two lines with *me* and *el*, *la*, *los* or *las*.
